```python
def policy(piles: list[int]) -> str:
    # Identify pile types
    big = -1      # index of a pile with size > 1 (-1 if none)
    n_big = 0     # number of piles with size > 1
    n_ones = 0    # number of piles with exactly 1
    first_one = -1
    largest = -1  # index of largest pile
    for i, p in enumerate(piles):
        if p > 1:
            n_big += 1
            big = i
        elif p == 1:
            n_ones += 1
            if first_one < 0:
                first_one = i
        if largest < 0 or p > piles[largest]:
            largest = i

    # Game already over (should not happen); return a dummy move.
    if largest < 0 or piles[largest] == 0:
        return "0,1"

    # Case 1: no pile bigger than 1 -> only singletons remain.
    if n_big == 0:
        return f"{first_one},1"

    # Case 2: exactly one big pile -> leave an odd number of singletons.
    if n_big == 1:
        if n_ones % 2 == 0:
            return f"{big},{piles[big] - 1}"  # leave it at 1
        return f"{big},{piles[big]}"          # take it entirely

    # Case 3: at least two big piles -> play normal Nim (move xor to 0).
    s = 0
    for p in piles:
        s ^= p
    if s:
        for i, p in enumerate(piles):
            t = p ^ s
            if t < p:
                return f"{i},{p - t}"
    # Xor already 0: losing against perfect play; stall by removing one
    # object from the largest pile to maximize opponent error chances.
    return f"{largest},1"
```
